newsitem.title: USA: NYC Giuliani has 10-point lead over Messinger-poll.
newsitem.headline: NYC Giuliani has 10-point lead over Messinger-poll.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani would beat his closest Democrat rival, Ruth Messinger, by 10 points if the November mayoral election were held on Wednesday, a survey by Quinnipiac College Poll found.

"Mayor Giuliani is riding high as his seemingly certain re-election approachs. And nothing--not his criticism from opponents, not the agonizing uncertainity over rent control, you name it, nothing seems to shake voters' judgment that he's doing a good job," said Maurice Carroll, the director of the polling institute, in prepared remarks.
The poll official noted Giuliani's approval rating has slipped from an all-time high hit in March, and now stands at 60 percent to 35 percent, with five percent undecided.

Manhattan Borough President Messinger was predicted to win the Democratic Primary, as she leads with 54 percent, beating both her rivals, City Council Member Sal Albanese and the Rev. Al Sharpton. They each captured 13 percent.

Giuliani would win handily against any of those candidates, the poll found, beating Messinger by 49 percent to 39 percent. But the survey found the strongest Democratic candidate enjoyed strong support from African Americans, who would back Messinger against Giuliani by 67 percent to 21 percent.
That was an even bigger margin than the lead Sharpton got, as 49 percent to 30 percent of blacks said they would vote for that candidate in a race with Giuliani.

"Just about everybody knows the Rev. Al Sharpton. But he's not popular," said the director of the polling institute. The survey also found that while 12 percent of those surveyed had favorable views of Sharpton, 54 percent had unfavorable opinions.
The Quinnipiac College surveyed 821 New York City residents who said they were registered voters from June 9 to 15. The margin of error was plus or minus 3.4 percent.
